newsitem.title: USA: Foreign chip trade in Japan increases to record.
newsitem.headline: Foreign chip trade in Japan increases to record.

text.p: The market share of non-Japanese computer chipmakers selling products in Japan rose to a record 32.6 percent in the first quarter, boosted by increased foreign access to the Japanese market and higher demand, according to the U.S. Trade Representative.

American, European and Asian chipmakers have been pushing for years to get a bigger share of the Japanese market, which had been particularly tough for foreign suppliers. Japan and the U.S. signed a new semiconductor trade accord last August.

"The increse in foreign share is a result of vigorous American competitiveness combined with a strong trade agreement on semiconductors between the U.S. and Japan," said George Scalise, president of U.S.-based Semiconductor Industry Association.

The first-quarter foreign share rose 3.2 percentage points to 32.6 percent from 29.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996, the SIA said. It also exceeds the prior all-time high of 29.6 percent that was set in the fourth quarter of 1995.
